title: A record parked at the pre-0.7.0 paused literal "Blocked" cannot leave that status by any command, and doctor reports the workspace healthy
description:
Reported by lore-web 2026-09-15 ~15:40Z against quest 0.7.0 (LWEB-80, paused by 0.6.x on 2026-09-09), ruled fleet-wide and ahead of QCLI-298/QCLI-297 by opum-agent 15:35Z; lore-cli has the same shape on LCLI-333, where it makes `lore check` exit 6 on their dev and blocks LCLI-504. This repository has no stranded record (QCLI-271 is Done; zero records at "Blocked").

REPRODUCED 2026-09-15 against the source build in a disposable workspace (default policy: statuses To Do/In Progress/Done, pausedStatus Paused), on a record hand-set to "Blocked": `task pause` -> validation "Illegal task transition: Blocked -> Paused."; `task start` -> "Illegal task transition: Blocked -> In Progress."; `task edit --status "In Progress"` and `task complete` -> "Task transition uses an unconfigured status."; `task edit --status Paused` -> "Task status is not configured."; `task demote --to "To Do"` -> "Illegal task demotion: Blocked has no earlier status to demote to."; `quest doctor --json` -> healthy true, no issues. Only `task archive` and non-status edits succeed, so the record can be retired or annotated but never resumed.

ROOT CAUSE. QCLI-287 renamed defaultLifecyclePolicy.pausedStatus from "Blocked" to "Paused" and pauseTask/startTask/legalDemoteTargets compare the record status to the configured value by exact string, so a record written under the old default became an ordinary unconfigured status on upgrade. QCLI-287 own notes predicted exactly this and recorded it as a release-notes callout; the CHANGELOG says "No transition ... changed", which was true of the code paths and false of a record already parked. The 0.7.0 CHANGELOG warning was published and the best-placed consumer (opum-cli-e2e suites/60) still missed it, so a warning is not the fix.

CLASSIFICATION: defect (start accepted the old paused literal in 0.6.x and does not in 0.7.0) plus the missing capability underneath it: doctor cannot see a record at an off-flow status at all.

SHAPE: the retired default literal "Blocked" is recognised by `task start` as a legacy paused status, only when it is neither on the configured ladder nor the configured pausedStatus, so a workspace that deliberately configures "Blocked" keeps 0.7.0 behaviour. `doctor` reports every record whose status is on neither the ladder nor the paused slot, naming the id, the status and the repair. No auto-migration and no silent rewrite: the exit is an explicit, attributed command.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `quest task start <id>` on a record whose status is the literal "Blocked" while the workspace pausedStatus is "Paused" and "Blocked" is on neither the ladder nor the paused slot returns kind task.started with status "In Progress", after which `task pause` parks it at "Paused"; proven by a CLI test that fails without the change and by a run of the source build on a hand-stranded record in a disposable workspace

`quest doctor --json` on a workspace holding an unrepaired record at an off-flow status (on neither the ladder nor the paused slot) returns healthy false with an issue naming the task id, the status, and the repair command; the same workspace returns healthy true after `task start` repairs it; covered by a test
A workspace that configures "Blocked" as its pausedStatus, or as a ladder status, behaves exactly as in 0.7.0: no retired-literal handling fires when the literal is configured; covered by a test

`quest task start --help`, the task-finalization guide, and the CHANGELOG (Fixed, under the release that ships it) name the retired literal, the exact repair command, and that nothing is migrated silently

The release that ships this is measured to be installable: the wrapper and all six platform packages resolve at the released version from the public registry, and lore-cli and lore-web are told with the exact repair command; post-publish evidence, so this criterion may close after the fix PR lands

plan: 1. Domain (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts): export the retired default paused literal; startTask accepts a record at that literal only when it is neither on the ladder nor the configured pausedStatus; export an off-flow predicate for doctor.

2. Doctor (src/application/planning/planning.ts + src/cli/main.ts): doctor takes the lifecycle policy, reports task_status_off_flow issues naming taskId, status and the repair hint; main passes the task service lifecycle.
3. Help and guides: task start help, doctor help, task-finalization guide name the retired literal and the repair.

4. Tests: domain (start from Blocked; configured Blocked keeps 0.7.0 behaviour), CLI semantics (hand-stranded record -> doctor unhealthy -> start -> doctor healthy -> pause -> Paused), planning doctor unit.

5. CHANGELOG Unreleased/Fixed with the repair command; bun run check; disposable-workspace run against the source build recorded as a note; PR into dev; close AC1-AC4 in the PR, AC5 after 0.7.1 publishes (separate release-prep task, QCLI-294 precedent).
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED AND RUN AGAINST THE SOURCE BUILD, 2026-09-15. Disposable workspace (scratchpad, git init, quest init, default policy), one record moved to In Progress and then hand-set to "Blocked" in the JSON to reproduce the bytes a 0.6.x pause wrote:
- before: quest doctor --json -> healthy false, issues [{code task_status_off_flow, taskId T-1, status Blocked, hint: "Blocked" is the paused status of an earlier release; `quest task start T-1 --actor <name> --actor-kind human` resumes it, and `quest task pause T-1` then parks it at "Paused".}]
- quest task start T-1 -> kind task.started, status In Progress
- after: quest doctor --json -> healthy true, issues []
- quest task pause T-1 -> kind task.paused, status Paused
- quest task start --help names the retired literal and that nothing migrates silently.

DESIGN CHOICES, stated so the next reader does not re-derive them.
1. The exit is `task start`, not a rename performed by `task pause`: start is what accepted the literal in 0.6.x, so this restores a transition rather than adding one, and pause keeps its single meaning (working -> paused).
2. Only the literal an earlier default actually wrote ("Blocked", exported as retiredPausedStatuses) is recognised, and only when the workspace configures it neither on the ladder nor as its paused status. A workspace that names "Blocked" itself keeps 0.7.0 behaviour exactly; any other unconfigured status is still refused by start. Tested both ways.
3. doctor checks ACTIVE records only (location "tasks"): the repair its hint names reaches active records alone, and a retained record at an off-flow status is retired, not stranded. Tested.
4. Additive envelope change only: project.doctor issues[] gains a second code, task_status_off_flow {taskId, status, hint}; milestone_task_not_found is unchanged and still sorts first. opum-cli-e2e suites/21 reads issues[] by code and suites/25 asserts determinism, neither locks the union closed (read on their origin/dev).
5. Composition uses defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy, so a workspace.toml [statuses] section does not reach the policy today; lore-web premise "no [statuses] section" is therefore the only case that exists. Not changed here.

VERIFIED BEFORE OPENING THE PR. bun run check: 506 pass, 0 fail (the single lint warning is the pre-existing one in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts). lore check: 63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Fails without the change, proven by stashing only src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts, src/application/planning/planning.ts and src/cli/main.ts and re-running the three touched test files: 3 fail (the new CLI test, the new doctor test, the new domain test), 24 pass; restored, 47 pass. AC1-AC4 checked on that evidence plus the source-build run in the previous note. AC5 stays open until 0.7.1 is on the registry; the release is its own task (QCLI-294 precedent) and this task stays In Progress until then, deliberately.
